'''Paul Malliavin''' ({{IPA|fr|maljavɛ̃|lang}}; September 10, 1925 &ndash; June 3, 2010) was a French [[mathematician]] who made important contributions to [[harmonic analysis]] and [[stochastic analysis]]. 
He is known for the [[Malliavin calculus]], an infinite-dimensional calculus for functionals on the [[Wiener space]], and his probabilistic proof of [[Hörmander's condition|Hörmander’s theorem]].
He was [[Professor]] at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] and a member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] from 1979 to 2010.<ref name=academie>{{cite web |url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/academie/membre/Malliavin_Paul.htm |title=In memoriam |date=June 3, 2010 |work=Academy of Sciences |language=French |accessdate=June 4, 2010 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120315164912/http://www.academie-sciences.fr/academie/membre/Malliavin_Paul.htm |archivedate=March 15, 2012 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Malliavin was the son of René Malliavin, also known as ''Michel Dacier'', a political writer and journalist, and Madeleine Delavenne, a physician. On 27 April 1965 he married [[Marie-Paule Malliavin|Marie-Paule Brameret]], who was also a mathematician and with whom he published several mathematical papers.<ref name="whoswho_fr">{{Cite web |title=Biographie Paul Malliavin |url=https://www.whoswho.fr/decede/biographie-paul-malliavin_15978 |language=French |accessdate=2023-10-04}}</ref><ref name="nachruf">{{Cite web |title=» Anciennes actualités – section: Marie-Paule Malliavin (1935-2019) |url=https://www.imj-prg.fr/blog/2020/10/21/anciennes-actualites/}}</ref> They had two children.<ref name="whoswho_fr" />

==Scientific contributions==

Malliavin's early work was in [[harmonic analysis]], where he derived important results on the spectral synthesis problem, providing definitive answers to fundamental questions in this field, including a complete characterization of 'band-limited' functions whose Fourier transform has compact support, known as the [[Beurling-Malliavin theorem]].<ref>
{{cite journal|last1=Beurling|first1=Arne|author-link=Arne Beurling|last2=Malliavin|first2=Paul|title=On Fourier transforms of measures with compact support|journal=Acta Mathematica|volume=107|year=1962|issue=3–4|pages=291–309|doi=10.1007/BF02545792|doi-access=free}}</ref>

In [[stochastic analysis]], Malliavin is known for his work on the stochastic calculus of variation, now known as the [[Malliavin calculus]], a mathematical theory which has found many applications in [[Monte Carlo simulation]] and [[mathematical finance]].

As stated by [[Daniel W. Stroock|Stroock]] and [[Marc Yor|Yor]]: "Like Norbert Wiener, Paul Malliavin came to probability theory from harmonic analysis, and, like Wiener, his analytic origins were apparent in everything he did there."<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Stroock|first1=Daniel|last2=Yor|first2=Marc|title=Remembering Paul Malliavin|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|volume=58|year=2011|pages=568|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201104/rtx110400568p.pdf}}</ref>
Malliavin introduced a differential operator on [[Wiener space]], now called the [[Malliavin derivative]], and derived an [[integration by parts]] formula for Wiener functionals. Using this integration by parts formula, Malliavin initiated a probabilistic approach to [[Hörmander's condition|Hörmander's theorem]] for hypo-elliptic operators and gave a condition for the existence of smooth densities for Wiener functionals in terms of their [[Malliavin covariance matrix]].
